analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 956-1003). It adds a description of an excluded startup "shape warmup" for ordinary EngineV2 slots: a 128-token probe run twice, optional shape cells, a 20 s wall budget, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0/always switch. I found no code changes in the supplied evidence, so no security control is weakened by this diff.

Threat-model relevance, per the documentation:
- The warmup is local-only and engine-internal. It trains no rates or counters and produces no served-request or output-token counters. It runs before registration or in the idle calibration session, and it is preempted by customer requests. The text states that IdleCalibrationCoordinator.beginForeground cancels it.
- The probes use synthetic prompts, not consumer data (A-001), so there is no new consumer-data exposure.
- Prefix-cache and SSD-checkpoint identity are unaffected, since sampling is not part of cache identity. T-041 is unchanged; the doc does not say the warmup probes donate to the SSD prefix cache. A later review of the implementation should check that warmup prompts are not persisted via the encrypted SSD tier (SSDPrefixCache.donate) and cannot create TTFT-oracle artifacts. This is unverified because the code is not in the supplied evidence.
- Availability (T-029, T-010): the warmup is bounded to 20 s, with at most three cell tries, and preemption leaves it due. The implementation of the bound and of preemption (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ShapeWarmup.swift) is not supplied, so the described behavior cannot be verified against code.
- The environment variable DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP is forwarded by the launchd job. It is an operator-controlled performance setting. The doc line 1193 notes unrecognized DARKBLOOM_* settings reject deadline qualification; confirm in code that the new variable is on the allowlist or classified correctly. This is a documentation-consistency question, not a finding.

The documentation also refers to a report file, ../reports/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md, which is not supplied. No finding qualifies.
